analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md, head lines 25-171 plus a media-discovery wording change near head 876. No code, config or deployment changes are supplied.

It documents unregistered, internal-only NemotronSuper local paths: bridge builder, load transaction, prompt contract, local image/text HTTP hook (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP), concurrency, prefill lane, prefix cache and MTP. Each is stated as not registered, with no public route and no production caller installing the hook.

Security-relevant claims the next pass should check against the source, which is not in this batch:
- The local HTTP hook is described as authenticated, defaults to absent, and is not installed by any production caller (relates to TB-003/TB-007).
- Media is accepted only as data:image/png|jpeg URIs, with ingress, media and decode charges before inspection and with container limits checked before raster allocation (DoS-related).
- The new NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1) is a resident in-memory recurrent checkpoint bank. It uses the 'local unscoped cache scope' and is not the encrypted SSD tier. Exposure is cross-request prefix reuse and a TTFT oracle (T-041/SEC-035) and must stay local-only. The threat model's statement that production never funds a resident-RAM prefix cache should be reconciled if this path is ever wired up. The doc says it is unregistered, so this is a documentation or threat-model gap rather than a regression.
- Client prompt-cache keys are rejected on this path, and the cache scope is unscoped, so cross-tenant reuse would apply if it were ever exposed to coordinator traffic.
- Optional MTP is gated on DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1 and is off by default.

The edit near head 876 references shared media discovery policy instead of vision_config. Its effect on the model template render check cannot be assessed from this text.

No finding is raised because everything described is explicitly unwired. Re-review is warranted if any later PR registers the model, installs the HTTP hook, or enables the memory prefix cache in production.
